subject: Conditional invoice release and PO attribute gating for staggered billing

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PO attribute gating for staggered invoice release

Hi Sara / Procurement team,

Thanks for sharing the draft PO. A quick item from our side before we sign: Asteria's PO is missing the attribute that drives our invoice-lane mapping (PO field: invoice_release_behavior). Without it, our billing system treats the PO as a single-shot invoice and will attempt to issue one consolidated invoice at month-end. For the staged billing you requested we need one of the following: 

- invoice_release_behavior: STAGGERED_MONTHLY
- or a line-item-level release date + milestone tags

Could you confirm which option Procurement can include in the PO? If neither is possible, we can accept a conditional workflow where Redwood splits invoices but requires an Authorization header (PO-ID + release token) on each invoice submission.

Also copying Vanessa from Billing to confirm operational constraints.

Next steps: please attach the final PO or confirm the attribute and desired net terms.

Thanks,

--
Priyom Das

2) If we add per-line release dates, is there a minimum granularity (e.g., monthly only, or can we do weekly)?

Sara —

Thanks for the quick reply. Answers inline: 

1) Authorization header approach: workable, but it will require Asteria to pass a release token in either the invoice submission through your ERP or in the payment remittance EDI. Operationally it increases AP overhead. If Procurement is open to a small process change, this is the fastest way to proceed without changing your PO template.

2) Granularity: our system supports both monthly and weekly release dates, but our recommended default is monthly to keep reconciliation simple. If you need weekly that is doable but we will push slightly higher bookkeeping on both sides.

Proposed compromise: Asteria issues the standard PO (we'll accept), Procurement adds line-item release dates using the format RELEASE_YYYYMM, OR confirm they will include the Authorization header on each invoice submission. If either path is provided, Redwood will align invoice cadence to the requested releases and honor net terms as negotiated.

I'm attaching: Asteria_PO_5421.pdf (your draft with highlighted line items) and a short invoice schedule proposal (Redwood-Invoice-Schedule-Proposal.xlsx). If helpful we can generate a short matrix for your ERP team showing where the release token can be passed.

Can Marissa (copies) help confirm the SLA and pre-authorized credit treatment?

Best,

--
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO attribute gating for staggered invoice release

Priyom / Marissa —

Operational notes from Billing: 

- If Procurement adds per-line RELEASE_YYYYMM, we can map automatically and issue invoices on the specified months. No additional AP header required.
- If Asteria wants to use Authorization header instead, we need a consistent token format and a point-of-contact at their ERP team to validate tokens on receipt. Token exchange will be handled via a signed micro-appendix to the SOW (we can do a short DocuSign).
- Net terms: Redwood will honor net30 by default. For staged invoices, payment timing will be per-invoice (i.e., clock starts on the invoice date for that tranche). We can't backdate payments across tranches.

Action items:
1) Priyom to confirm which path Asteria prefers.
2) If Authorization header, send POC for ERP and we'll prepare micro-appendix DocuSign.
3) If per-line release dates, Procurement to send updated PO with RELEASE_YYYYMM tags.

Vanessa Ortiz
Billing Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Next steps agreed: 
- Procurement to provide the ERP POC (name + email) by EOD Friday 6/18.
- Redwood to draft micro-appendix and DocuSign link for signature (attached: docusign-Asteria-SOW-link.txt — placeholder to be replaced with live link once the micro-appendix is ready).
- Once signed, Redwood will accept the PO as-is and start issuing tranche invoices per the release tokens. Net terms remain net30 per invoice.

I appreciate you moving fast on this. If Procurement prefers the per-line RELEASE_YYYYMM route instead, we can switch — but that will require Procurement to re-issue an updated PO before we begin billing.

Thanks,
